alerts.title: TDF toxicity: abdominal pain
alerts.message: Guidelines list abdominal pain or discomfort and decreased appetite as recognised TDF toxicity presentations, prompting LFTs and RFTs with possible substitution to ABC if deranged. Patient on TDF since March 2023 presents with abdominal pain. Appetite is preserved and there is no fever, which argues against severe hepatotoxicity or lactic acidosis but does not exclude early TDF-related renal or metabolic toxicity. Non-drug causes such as intercurrent gastrointestinal infection should also be considered.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform LFTs and RFTs (including eGFR). If deranged, substitute TDF with ABC per guidelines.

alerts.title: Annual TDF renal monitoring overdue
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR every 12 months for ART-experienced patients on TDF. Patient has been on TDF since March 2023 and the only creatinine on record is from November 2025. No renal function test was ordered at today's visit despite presentation with abdominal pain, a recognised TDF toxicity symptom. Annual renal monitoring is now due.

evidence.recommended_action: Order serum creatinine and eGFR today to fulfil annual TDF monitoring requirements.

alerts.title: Annual viral load monitoring due
alerts.message: Guidelines specify routine viral load monitoring 12 months after ART initiation and annually thereafter for adults. Patient initiated ART in March 2023; the last viral load of 25 copies/mL was done in November 2025. No viral load was ordered at today's January 2026 visit. While the most recent result confirms suppression, annual scheduling should be maintained.

evidence.recommended_action: Confirm next routine viral load is scheduled within 12 months of the November 2025 result.

A patient who has been on ART for more than 6 months and is responding to ART is considered virally suppressed at VL <200 copies/mL and <400 copies/mL for plasma and DBS samples, respectively. Facilities should constitute a multidisciplinary VL review committees to review, track, and make decisions to optimize ART regimen by switching to second-line, third- line, or a more potent regimen.
